source_english_abstract: The lack of data can be an issue at the beginning of a study on new historical handwritten documents. To solve this issue, we present the decoder part of a multimodal approach based on transductive transfer learning for transcripting play titles of the Italian Comedy.
query_text: We address transcribing handwritten play titles from 18th-century Italian Comedy financial registers without annotated training data. Using a multimodal encoder-decoder with transductive transfer learning, we convert character n-gram vectors into text sequences via GRU. Leveraging contemporary and cross-domain resources for this multilingual (Italian/French) setting, we achieved 97.27% character accuracy and 86.57% word accuracy, despite only 67.58% vocabulary overlap with the training data.

source_english_abstract: Medical area is integral part of our lives due to health concerns, but the availability of medical information does not guarantee its correct understanding by patients. Several studies addressed this issue and pointed out real difﬁculty in understanding of health contents by patients. We propose to use eye-tracking methods for studying further the issue and for detecting which linguistic units in health documents are problematic. For this, original and simpliﬁed versions of medical documents are exploited. Eye-tracking permits to follow the gaze of participants and to reveal reading indicators such as duration of ﬁxations, regressions and saccades. The results indicate that there is statistically signiﬁcant difference in reading of original and simpliﬁed versions of the health documents tested.
query_text: This study investigates how lexical simplification impacts comprehension of complex French clinical documents in radiology and cardiology. Using eye-tracking to measure fixation duration, regressions, and saccades, we will identify specific linguistic units causing cognitive processing blocks. By testing fifty non-expert participants on original versus simplified versions, we aim to demonstrate statistically significant differences in reading indicators, confirming that targeted simplification effectively reduces reading difficulties and enhances patient understanding of medical information.

source_english_abstract: This article concerns the detection of attitudes – i.e affects, appreciations and jugements (Martin & White, 2005) – in the user’s verbal content during a face-to-face interaction with an embodied conversational agent. It tackles the issue of the adaptation to the ECA’s communicational goals and to the conversational speech. After a description of our theoretical model, it introduces an annotation model dedicated to the study of attitudes in a human-agent interaction corpus. Then, it describes a ﬁrst version of our detection system, focusing on the attitude which can refer to a user’s like or dislike. The system is rule-based and embeds logic and semantic representations of the sentences.
query_text: How can we detect user attitudes in verbal content during face-to-face interactions with embodied conversational agents, adapting to communicational goals? Propose an annotation model and a first detection system version focused on user preferences for social relation management.

query_text: This research investigates how an interactive virtual agent can perceive human conversational attitudes during face-to-face spoken dialogues. The proposed framework combines a dedicated annotation scheme with a symbolic rule-based system that parses utterance semantics to recognize expressions of approval, criticism, or personal preference, allowing the virtual character to adapt appropriately.

source_english_abstract: Geometry of self-attention in classification: when geometry replaces attention Various studies have highlighted the anisotropy of BERT word embeddings within an utterance, i.e., their concentration in a given direction, especially in a classification task. In this paper, we aim at better understanding this phenomenon and how this convergence is built by analyzing the geometric properties of the word embeddings, keys and values within a self-attention layer. We show that the direction towards which embeddings align themselves characterizes class membership. We then study the intrinsic mechanism of the self-attention layer and the mechanisms at play between keys and values to ensure the construction of an anisotropic representation. This construction is progressive when several layers are stacked. It also proves to be robust to external constraints on the distribution of attention weights, which the model compensates through the values and keys.
query_text: Investigate how stacked transformer encoders develop directional bias in token representations for categorical prediction. Analyze the internal projection matrices to reveal how the model constructs class-specific alignment while compensating for normalization constraints. This geometric study explains how the architecture maintains distinct semantic directions across layers, ensuring robust feature separation despite inherent representational limitations in the attention mechanism.

source_english_abstract: Clinical cases classiﬁcation and automatic evaluation of student answers : Presentation of the DEFT 2021 Challenge DEFT is an annual French-speaking text mining challenge. We present the corpora, tasks, and baselines we produced : (i) identify the clinical proﬁle of patients described in clinical cases, (ii) au- tomatically assess student answers from online survey (Moodle) based on the teacher’s correction, and (iii) continue to evaluate student answers based on answers already assessed by the teacher. Results ranged from 0.394 to 0.814 F-score on the ﬁrst task (7 participants), 0.448 to 0.682 accuracy on the second one (3 participants), and 0.133 to 0.510 accuracy on the last one (3 participants).
query_text: How can clinical profiles be identified from patient cases and student answers in online questionnaires be automatically evaluated based on teacher corrections? What are the typical performance ranges for these tasks, specifically regarding precision-recall harmonic means for clinical identification and accuracy metrics for evaluating student responses?

source_english_abstract: This paper presents an unsupervised approach for Natural Language Generation within the framework of question-answering task. This approach aims at solving the too-short or too-long answer generation problem without requiring annotated data. The proposed approach shows promising results for both English and French.
query_text: An unsupervised method leverages transformer architectures and dependency parsing to reformulate questions into concise, natural language responses. By avoiding the need for annotated question-answer pairs, this approach generates appropriately sized answers in multiple languages. Evaluations using large-scale knowledge bases and universal dependency treebanks demonstrate promising results for producing fluent, length-controlled outputs without relying on supervised training data.

source_english_abstract: This paper presents methods to perform knowledge extraction from very large databases of WEB chat conversations between operators and clients in customer contact centers. Extracting knowledge from chat corpus is a challenging research issue. Simply applying traditional text mining tools is clearly sub-optimal as it takes into account neither the interaction dimension nor the particular nature of this language which shares properties of both spoken and written language. We present a method predicting users satisfaction in a chat-based service trained on answers from users to satisfaction surveys.
query_text: A system automatically predicts customer satisfaction from extensive web chat logs by training on direct post-interaction survey responses. This approach estimates quality indicators from transcripts, demonstrating the feasibility of supervised prediction on massive corpora. It enables real-time monitoring and addresses non-respondent cases, effectively leveraging direct user annotations to assess service quality across various technical and commercial topics.

source_english_abstract: Clinical trials are very important for the evaluation of new therapies or diagnosis procedures, of their security and efﬁcency. They must rely on convenient sample of the population. the challenge is then to recruit sufﬁcient number of participants with similar characteristics to guarantee that the results are controlled and due tu the factors studied. This is a difﬁcult task, mainly performed manuelly. Because numerical values are frequent and provide important information, we propose an automatic system that aims their extraction and normalization.
query_text: A system leveraging conditional random fields with boundary tagging for entity recognition, integrated with rule-based unit normalization, is proposed. This approach targets unstructured medical trial documents to extract and standardize numerical data from inclusion and exclusion criteria. The goal is to create a specialized annotated corpus and an automated extraction tool, thereby mitigating recruitment delays by facilitating the precise identification of patient eligibility parameters within complex textual protocols.

This approach enables real-time monitoring of interaction outcomes by learning from post-session annotations, addressing missing data challenges. The method validates the feasibility of deriving performance metrics from raw conversational transcripts, facilitating proactive quality assurance in high-volume digital support environments without relying on manual review.

source_english_abstract: To determine whether some often-used lexical association measures assign high scores to n-grams that chance could have produced as frequently as observed, we used an extension of Fisher’s exact test to sequences longer than two words to analyse a corpus of four million words. The results, based on the precision-recall curve and the average precision, show that simple-ll is extremely effective. MI3 is more efﬁcient than the other hypothesis tests-based measures and even reaches a performance level almost equal to simple-ll for trigrams.
query_text: How can statistical significance testing for multi-word expressions be extended beyond bigrams using Monte-Carlo permutation methods? Specifically, analyze a large-scale corpus of spontaneous spoken language to evaluate the robustness of these extended tests in identifying significant n-grams within natural conversational data.

query_text: Recruiting suitable patient cohorts for medical research requires screening complex eligibility criteria that heavily depend on quantitative thresholds. Because these quantitative parameters are typically assessed by hand, this project introduces an automated method to identify, extract, and standardize numerical values and their associated measurement units from unstructured medical protocol descriptions.

source_english_abstract: Endogeneous methods are important for the graph based knowledge resource building. In the fra- mework of the experiment we describe in the present paper, we focus on inferring new relations. In particular, we consider semantic relation and sense reﬁnement inference. Various mecanisms of semantic relation inference including those with term polysemy have been detailed by Zarrouk (2015) in the monolingual context. To our knowledge, no experimental work have been done in order to elaborate such methods for a multilingual resource enhancement.
query_text: How can multilingual lexico-semantic resources be enhanced by inferring semantic relations and sense refinements for under-resourced languages using endogenous methods? This approach proposes a novel experimental framework for multilingual relation inference, specifically addressing the gap in existing monolingual-only approaches for resource enhancement.

source_english_abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for automatic summarization based on a genetic algorithm that explores candidate summaries space following an objective function computed over ngrams probability distributions of the candidate sum- mary and the source documents. This method does not consider a summary as a stack of independant sentences but as a whole text. We compare this method to one of the best existing methods which is based on integer linear programming, and show its efﬁciency on TAC 2009 corpus.
query_text: Rather than treating an abridgement as an isolated collection of ranked sentences, this approach formulates document condensation as a global optimization problem over whole texts. An evolutionary search strategy explores candidate passages guided by an objective that minimizes divergence between word sequence distributions in the generated text and the source documents.

source_english_abstract: Person role recognition in video broadcasts consists in classifying people into roles such as anchor, journalist, guest, etc. Existing approaches mostly consider one modality, either audio (speaker role recognition) or image (shot role recognition), ﬁrstly because of the non-synchrony between both modalities, and secondly because of the lack of a video corpus annotated in both modalities. Deep Neural Networks (DNN) approaches offer the ability to learn simultaneously feature representations (embeddings) and classiﬁcation functions. This paper presents a multimodal fusion of audio, text and image embeddings spaces for speaker role recognition in asynchronous data. Monomodal embeddings are trained on exogenous data and ﬁne-tuned using a DNN on 70 hours of French Broadcasts corpus for the target task. Experiments on the REPERE corpus show the beneﬁt of the embeddings level fusion compared to the monomodal embeddings systems and to the standard late fusion method.
query_text: Does embedding-level fusion of monomodal representations, specifically using convolutional networks for text and deep neural networks for audio or image data, outperform both monomodal systems and standard late fusion methods for speaker role recognition? This approach involves fine-tuning the fused multimodal embeddings on target task data to enhance overall performance.

Focus on English clinical trial protocols from a major public registry, specifically targeting inclusion and exclusion criteria. The annotation should capture concepts, values, units, and quantifiers to support automated extraction of numerical data from unstructured text.

This research investigates internal graph inference to deduce novel semantic links and finer word sense distinctions. By leveraging existing connectivity patterns within the network topology itself, the method expands relational coverage without relying on outside manual resources.

This approach targets eligibility specifications in public trial registries, creating a specialized annotated dataset. The system aims to accelerate subject identification by automating the parsing of structured data from free text, thereby reducing administrative bottlenecks in the research workflow.

source_english_abstract: This paper describes the Nantalco team's participation in task 2 of the DEFT contest in 2021: Automatic evaluation of students' answers based on an existing reference. We mainly used features based on the cosine similarity of the two vectors representing the textual similarity between student responses and the reference. Several types of vectors were used (count vector, tf-idf vector, non- contextualized embeddings from fastText, contextualized embeddings from Camembert and fine- tuned Multilingual Sentence Embeddings). The best performance of the contest on this task was 0.682 (precision). The maximum performance of our team (0.639) was obtained with the Multilingual Sentence Embeddings, while the best performance of raw embeddings of CamemBERT was only 0.55, suggesting that recent pre-trained language models need to be fine-tuned in order to have adequate embeddings at the sentence level.
query_text: How does fine-tuning multilingual embeddings improve the precision of automatic student answer evaluation using textual similarity? Specifically, what are the performance gains compared to raw pre-trained models, and why is fine-tuning necessary to achieve superior results in measuring semantic alignment between student responses and reference answers?
